decls.description: What an issuer's status list says of a credential (the status types of the IETF Token Status List).

One entry of a trust list: this issuer may state this attribute, from a day until (exclusive) another. Origin: the trust list as its keeper published it, pinned by its hash (a vendor fact, Q8); the in port refuses a list whose bytes differ from the pin. A rule cannot derive it: who may state what is the keeper's choice. Needed by question 6: on whose authority does the municipality rely on a claim? A changed authority is a new entry with its own days, never an edit, so a conclusion keeps the ground it had. Rules cannot read a date yet, so each date has its day number beside it.

slots.description: For `same_subject` only: the node whose identifiers the entry lets its issuer name (Y4.15). An entry without a node covers none; a statement is authorised only when an entry covers each node it names.

decls.description: A credential as its holder presented it: who issued it, about whom, on which day. Origin: an observation, the presentation as received; the in port verified the issuer's signature and refuses one changed byte. A rule cannot derive what another party stated. Needed by question 6. Its subject is a person only by a `p-` identifier; no personal attribute is stored here.

slots.description: The person the credential is about, by the issuer's own identifier (local to the issuer's node).

decls.description: One attribute the municipality asked of a presented credential, with its value when the holder disclosed it. Origin: an observation, the presentation as received: a disclosed value is one whose digest the issuer signed. Closed world over the presentation: a claim without a value was not disclosed, and what it would say is unknown (reason not_disclosed), never empty and never false. Needed by question 6.

slots.description: The disclosed value; absent when the holder did not disclose it.

decls.description: A signed statement that two identifiers, each at a node of its own, name one person (W4 step 2, K20; Y4.2). Origin: an observation, the statement as received; the in port verified its issuer's signature and refuses one changed byte. A rule cannot derive it: that two identifiers name one person is what a register states, and equal or equal-looking identifiers never say it. Whether the statement's issuer is the authority for that identity is a rule (rules/credentials.dl), from the trust list, never a field here. Needed by question 7. The two identifiers are in no order; a rule reads the statement both ways round.

slots.description: The person's identifier at the first node.
The person's identifier at the second node.

decls.description: What the issuer's status list said of a credential or an identity statement on the day it was looked up. Origin: an observation, the status list as the issuer signed it, looked up by the in port. A rule cannot derive whether an issuer revoked what it issued. Closed world: the lookups are all there are, so a credential or a statement without a lookup that found it valid is not in good standing. A lookup is of exactly one of the two (the invariant status_lookup_not_of_one). Needed by questions 6 and 7.

slots.description: The credential looked up; absent when the lookup is of a statement.
The identity statement looked up; absent when the lookup is of a credential.

lines: // Which claim of another organisation the municipality relies on (W4, K19). A claim enters
// as an observation (written by the credential in port, which verified its signature).
// That the municipality relies on it is a conclusion of three grounds established apart from each other:
// the issuer's statement, the issuer's authority for that attribute on the day of issuance, and
// the credential's status. Authority is derived, never configured (Y4.10). Below the claims: which identifiers of
// two nodes name one person, and so what the municipality relies on about a person it knows by its own identifier.
// The issuer of a claim's credential was on the trust list for the claim's attribute on the day it issued the
// credential. Grounds: the credential (issuer, day of issuance) and a trust entry (issuer, attribute, days), from
// two sources: the presentation and the pinned trust list.
.decl issuer_authorised(claim: symbol, entry: symbol)

issuer_authorised(k, e) :- credential_claim__credential(k, c), credential_claim__attribute(k, a), credential__issuer(c, i), credential__issued_on_day(c, t), trust_entry__issuer(e, i), trust_entry__attribute(e, a), trust_entry__valid_from_day(e, f), trust_entry__valid_until_day(e, u), f <= t, t < u.
.decl authorised(claim: symbol)
authorised(k) :- issuer_authorised(k, _).
// A lookup of the issuer's status list found the credential revoked or suspended.
.decl status_withdrawn(credential: symbol)
status_withdrawn(c) :- status_lookup__credential(s, c), status_lookup__status(s, "revoked").
status_withdrawn(c) :- status_lookup__credential(s, c), status_lookup__status(s, "suspended").
// A lookup found the credential valid, and no lookup found it revoked or suspended. Grounds: the status lookups,
// a source of their own (the issuer's signed status list).
.decl in_good_standing(credential: symbol)
in_good_standing(c) :- status_lookup__credential(s, c), status_lookup__status(s, "valid"), !status_withdrawn(c).
// The holder disclosed the claim's value. The presentation is complete (closed world): a requested claim
// without a value was not disclosed.
.decl disclosed(claim: symbol)
disclosed(k) :- credential_claim__value(k, _).
.decl not_disclosed(claim: symbol)
not_disclosed(k) :- credential_claim(k), !disclosed(k).
// The outcome per claim: `known` when all three grounds hold; otherwise `unknown`, with each reason that
// applies. A claim that was not disclosed is unknown, never absent and never false.
// @outcome credential_claim
.decl claim_assessment(claim: symbol, state: symbol, reason: symbol)
claim_assessment(k, "unknown", "not_disclosed") :- not_disclosed(k).
claim_assessment(k, "unknown", "issuer_not_authorised") :- credential_claim(k), !authorised(k).
claim_assessment(k, "unknown", "status_not_valid") :- credential_claim__credential(k, c), !in_good_standing(c).
claim_assessment(k, "known", "") :- disclosed(k), authorised(k), credential_claim__credential(k, c), in_good_standing(c).
// What the municipality relies on: a person has an attribute with a value. It reads the `known` row, so its
// proof reaches the three independent grounds: the disclosed claim (the presentation), the trust entry (the
// trust list) and the status lookup (the issuer's status list). None of them alone gives it. The person is the
// issuer's own identifier, local to the issuer's node (Y4.12), so the node is part of the conclusion: the same
// characters at two issuers are two persons until a register states otherwise (K20).
.decl attested(node: symbol, subject: symbol, attribute: symbol, value: symbol)

attested(n, p, a, v) :- claim_assessment(k, "known", ""), credential_claim__credential(k, c), credential__issuer(c, n), credential__subject(c, p), credential_claim__attribute(k, a), credential_claim__value(k, v).
// Identity across nodes (W4 step 2, K20; Y4.2). Two identifiers of two nodes name one person only by a signed
// statement of the register that is the authority for that identity. Equal or equal-looking identifiers join
// nothing: no rule in this pack compares one identifier with another.
// A statement names two identifiers, each at its node, in no order: it is read both ways round.
.decl stated(statement: symbol, node: symbol, identifier: symbol, other_node: symbol, other_identifier: symbol)
stated(s, n, x, m, y) :- identity_statement__first_node(s, n), identity_statement__first_identifier(s, x), identity_statement__second_node(s, m), identity_statement__second_identifier(s, y).
stated(s, m, y, n, x) :- identity_statement__first_node(s, n), identity_statement__first_identifier(s, x), identity_statement__second_node(s, m), identity_statement__second_identifier(s, y).
// An authority is for something (Y4.15): a trust entry for `same_subject` names the node whose identifiers its
// issuer may name, and an entry without a node covers none. Entry e lets the statement's issuer name identifiers of
// node n, and its window holds the day the issuer states. Grounds: the statement (issuer, day it states) and a
// trust entry (issuer, attribute, node, days), from two sources: the statement and the pinned trust list.
.decl statement_scope(statement: symbol, node: symbol, entry: symbol)

statement_scope(s, n, e) :- identity_statement__issuer(s, i), identity_statement__issued_on_day(s, t), trust_entry__issuer(e, i), trust_entry__attribute(e, "same_subject"), trust_entry__node(e, n), trust_entry__valid_from_day(e, f), trust_entry__valid_until_day(e, u), f <= t, t < u.
// An issuer's date alone proves no time (Y4.15): entry e covers the statement at node n on the day of lookup l,
// a day on which the node itself held the statement (the lookup is keyed by the index inside it), when the window
// also holds that day: valid_from <= issued_on <= looked_up_on < valid_until. Grounds: the scope above and the
// node's own lookup, a source of its own (the issuer's status list as the node read it, on a declared day).
.decl statement_covered(statement: symbol, node: symbol, entry: symbol, lookup: symbol)

statement_covered(s, n, e, l) :- statement_scope(s, n, e), identity_statement__issued_on_day(s, t), trust_entry__valid_until_day(e, u), status_lookup__statement(l, s), status_lookup__looked_up_on_day(l, d), t <= d, d < u.
// The statement is authorised: on the day of one lookup, an entry of its issuer covers each of the two nodes it
// names. So its proof reaches both entries and the lookup.
.decl statement_authorised(statement: symbol, first_entry: symbol, second_entry: symbol, lookup: symbol)
statement_authorised(s, e, g, l) :- identity_statement__first_node(s, n), identity_statement__second_node(s, m), statement_covered(s, n, e, l), statement_covered(s, m, g, l).
.decl authoritative(statement: symbol)
authoritative(s) :- statement_authorised(s, _, _, _).
// On the issuer's day, an entry names each node the statement names: the issuer's word alone would let it.
.decl scoped(statement: symbol)
scoped(s) :- identity_statement__first_node(s, n), identity_statement__second_node(s, m), statement_scope(s, n, _), statement_scope(s, m, _).
// The node looked the statement up at least once.
.decl statement_seen(statement: symbol)
statement_seen(s) :- status_lookup__statement(_, s).
// A lookup of the issuer's status list found the statement revoked or suspended.
.decl statement_withdrawn(statement: symbol)
statement_withdrawn(s) :- status_lookup__statement(l, s), status_lookup__status(l, "revoked").
statement_withdrawn(s) :- status_lookup__statement(l, s), status_lookup__status(l, "suspended").
// A lookup found the statement valid, and no lookup found it revoked or suspended. Grounds: the status lookups,
// a source of their own (the issuer's signed status list).
.decl statement_in_good_standing(statement: symbol)
statement_in_good_standing(s) :- status_lookup__statement(l, s), status_lookup__status(l, "valid"), !statement_withdrawn(s).
// Two identifiers of two nodes name one person: the `same-as` of the identity theory (G02). Grounds, established
// apart from each other: the register's signed statement, its issuer's authority for each of the two nodes
// (two trust entries of the trust list) on the issuer's day and on the node's own lookup day, and its status (the
// issuer's status list). None of them alone gives it.
.decl same_subject(node: symbol, identifier: symbol, other_node: symbol, other_identifier: symbol)
same_subject(n, x, m, y) :- stated(s, n, x, m, y), statement_authorised(s, _, _, _), statement_in_good_standing(s).
// The statements that name a credential's subject (its issuer's identifier, at its issuer's node) beside an
// identifier of the municipality's own node. A statement of the same characters at another node does not name it.
.decl names_here(credential: symbol, statement: symbol, person: symbol)
names_here(c, s, p) :- credential__issuer(c, n), credential__subject(c, x), stated(s, n, x, "https://municipality.invented.example", p).
.decl named_here(credential: symbol)
named_here(c) :- names_here(c, _, _).
// The municipality's own identifier for a credential's subject: a join across two nodes that reads same_subject
// and nothing else about identity.
.decl identified(credential: symbol, person: symbol)
identified(c, p) :- credential__issuer(c, n), credential__subject(c, x), same_subject(n, x, "https://municipality.invented.example", p).
.decl is_identified(credential: symbol)
is_identified(c) :- identified(c, _).
// The outcome per credential: `known` when a statement that holds names its subject beside an identifier
// of the municipality; otherwise `unknown`, with the reason of each statement that names it, or that none does.
// Without a statement the join is unknown, never a match by equal identifiers and never "another person". An
// issuer whose entries name both nodes on its own day, but whose window held no day on which the node looked the
// statement up, gets a reason of its own: what helps is a new statement of the present authority.
// @outcome credential
.decl subject_identification(credential: symbol, state: symbol, reason: symbol)
subject_identification(c, "unknown", "no_identity_statement") :- credential(c), !named_here(c).
subject_identification(c, "unknown", "statement_issuer_not_authorised") :- names_here(c, s, _), !is_identified(c), !scoped(s).
subject_identification(c, "unknown", "statement_issuance_not_established") :- names_here(c, s, _), !is_identified(c), scoped(s), statement_seen(s), !authoritative(s).
subject_identification(c, "unknown", "statement_status_not_valid") :- names_here(c, s, _), !is_identified(c), !statement_in_good_standing(s).
subject_identification(c, "known", "") :- identified(c, _).
// What the municipality relies on about a person it knows by its own identifier: a claim another node attested
// of its own identifier, joined across the two nodes only through same_subject. Its proof combines two sets of
// independent grounds: the claim's (the presentation, the trust list, the issuer's status list) and the
// identity's (the register's statement, the trust list, the register's status list).
.decl attested_here(person: symbol, attribute: symbol, value: symbol)
attested_here(p, a, v) :- subject_identification(c, "known", ""), identified(c, p), credential__issuer(c, n), credential__subject(c, x), attested(n, x, a, v).
// A status lookup is of exactly one credential or one identity statement; the in port writes one of the two.
.decl looked_up(lookup: symbol)
looked_up(l) :- status_lookup__credential(l, _).
looked_up(l) :- status_lookup__statement(l, _).
// @invariant
.decl status_lookup_not_of_one(lookup: symbol)
status_lookup_not_of_one(l) :- status_lookup(l), !looked_up(l).
status_lookup_not_of_one(l) :- status_lookup__credential(l, _), status_lookup__statement(l, _).
.output claim_assessment, attested, same_subject, subject_identification, attested_here

module.description: What another organisation states, as the municipality receives it (W4, K19 and K20): a trust list that says which issuer may state which attribute, the credentials holders present, statements that two identifiers of two nodes name one person, and lookups of the issuers' status lists. Entirely synthetic: the issuers and nodes are invented and say so in their names and titles, and a person is only a `p-` identifier, local to the node that gave it (Y4.12). The credential in port (edge/plugins/credential-in) verifies every signature, disclosure and pin, and writes these as observations with their sources (facts/credentials.yaml). That the municipality relies on a claim, and that two identifiers name one person, are conclusions of rules/credentials.dl, never a field here.
